title: Islamic Practices and Health
subtitle: What science supports and which health claims to avoid
summary: Islam joins worship of Allah with care for the body, restraint, and avoiding harm. Studies support gains, but do not prove Islam.

seo.metaTitle: Islamic Practices and Health: What Science Supports
seo.metaDescription: A concise, evidence-based review of prayer, fasting, alcohol, gambling, cleanliness, miswak, breastfeeding, exercise, and other Islamic health practices.

sections.title: Evidence and Limits
sections.body: Islam directs worship to Allah. It also treats the body as a trust and forbids avoidable harm. Research may support a practice. It cannot prove a religion by itself. Sound evidence is welcome. Exaggeration is not.

sections.title: Prayer and Quran
sections.body:
Quran 13:28 links remembrance of Allah with a reassured heart. Salah combines worship, recitation, attention, and movement. Reviews report possible reductions in anxiety and stress. Studies are often small. Salah is not simply Islamic meditation. It does not replace mental-health care.

- [Review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36119448/)
- [Review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37408452/)

sections.title: Ramadan Fasting
sections.body:
Quran 2:183 says fasting develops taqwa, or awareness of Allah. A review found modest short-term gains in weight, blood pressure, blood fats, and glucose during Ramadan. Results vary with health, diet, sleep, and climate. Quran 2:185 exempts the sick and travelers.

- [Review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38335125/)
- [Review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36725794/)

sections.title: Avoiding Alcohol
sections.body:
Quran 5:90 commands believers to avoid intoxicants. WHO describes alcohol as toxic and dependence-producing. It causes many health and social harms. Islam's ban protects mind, body, family, and society.

- [WHO](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/alcohol)
- [WHO](https://www.who.int/europe/news-room/04-01-2023-no-level-of-alcohol-consumption-is-safe-for-our-health)

sections.title: Avoiding Gambling
sections.body:
Quran 5:90 prohibits gambling. The surrounding passage explains that it creates hostility and distracts from prayer. WHO links gambling with debt, family breakdown, violence, mental illness, and suicide. Islam closes this door before addiction spreads.

- [WHO](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/gambling)

sections.title: Moderation in Eating
sections.body:
Quran 7:31 says to eat and drink without excess. This agrees with health advice on balance and moderation. Obesity has many causes. The verse should never shame people. It teaches gratitude, restraint, and less waste.

- [WHO](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/healthy-diet)
- [WHO](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/obesity-and-overweight)

sections.title: Cleanliness and Wudu
sections.body:
The Quran makes washing before prayer part of Muslim life. Soap-and-water handwashing reduces diarrheal and respiratory illness. This is not a trial of wudu. Wudu often uses water without soap and has a spiritual purpose. It supports, but does not replace, hygiene and treatment.

- [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/clean-hands/data-research/facts-stats/)
- [WHO](https://www.who.int/tools/elena/review-summaries/wsh-diarrhoea--hand-washing-promotion-for-preventing-diarrhoea)

sections.title: Miswak and Oral Health
sections.body:
The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ encouraged the siwak around prayer (Sahih al-Bukhari 887). A review found that miswak can work like a toothbrush for plaque and gingivitis, although studies did not report technique and frequency consistently. Clean technique and regular use matter. It does not replace dental treatment.

- [Review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35944735/)
- [Review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33513418/)

sections.title: Breastfeeding
sections.body:
The Quran recognizes breastfeeding for up to two years. It assigns costs to the father and allows earlier weaning by mutual consent. WHO recommends six months of exclusive breastfeeding, then foods while breastfeeding continues. The verse teaches compassionate care, not judgment of mothers.

- [WHO](https://www.who.int/health-topics/breastfeeding)
- [WHO](https://cdn.who.int/media/docs/default-source/nutrition-and-food-safety/complementary-feeding/cf-guidelines/systematic-review-continued-breastfeeding.pdf)

sections.title: Sex and Marriage
sections.body:
Islam confines sex to marriage and prohibits approaching zina in Al-Isra 17:32. This joins intimacy to commitment, rights, and repentance. CDC guidance identifies complete abstinence as the surest way to prevent sexual transmission of infections while it is maintained. Testing and mutual monogamy also reduce risk.

- [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/sti/prevention/index.html)

sections.title: Circumcision
sections.body:
Authentic hadith identify circumcision as part of fitrah, or natural cleanliness (Sahih al-Bukhari 5889). WHO-reviewed trials found that voluntary medical circumcision cuts heterosexual HIV acquisition by men by about 60 percent in high-burden settings. This is partial protection, not immunity. It should be done safely.

- [WHO](https://www.who.int/teams/global-hiv-hepatitis-and-stis-programmes/hiv/prevention/voluntary-medical-male-circumcision)

sections.title: Gratitude
sections.body:
Gratitude to Allah is central to worship, and the Quran connects thankfulness with increase. A meta-analysis linked gratitude exercises with modest improvements in mental health, while study methods and results varied. Islamic shukr recognizes the Giver. It does not deny grief or cure illness.

- [Meta-analysis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37585888/)

sections.title: Community
sections.body:
Congregational prayer, family ties, visiting the sick, charity, and neighborly care make connection part of Muslim life. Research links loneliness and isolation with worse health and higher mortality. This does not prove that mosque attendance alone causes longer life. It supports the wisdom of making care a duty.

- [U.S. Surgeon General](https://www.hhs.gov/surgeongeneral/reports-and-publications/connection/index.html)
- [Review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37337095/)

sections.title: Rest and Sleep
sections.body:
The Prophet ﷺ taught that ‘your body has a right over you’ when correcting worship that neglected sleep and family duties (Sahih al-Bukhari 5199). Research links very short and very long sleep with poorer outcomes. Needs vary. Evidence has not proved one Sunnah sleep schedule. Islam encourages balance.

- [Review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28889101/)

sections.title: Movement
sections.body:
Salah includes standing, bowing, prostrating, and sitting. These movements interrupt stillness, but prayer is not a full workout. WHO recommends aerobic activity and muscle training to reduce disease and depression. Prayer nourishes worship. Muslims should also maintain strength as able.

- [WHO](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/physical-activity)

sections.title: Avoiding Tobacco
sections.body:
Tobacco is not named in the Quran because it was unknown in seventh-century Arabia. Muslim rulings apply principles against self-harm, harm to others, addiction, and waste. WHO says tobacco harms nearly every organ and kills over seven million people yearly. Islamic principles address this later danger.

- [WHO](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/tobacco)

sections.title: Claims to Avoid
sections.body:
No reliable human evidence shows that ordinary gold jewelry lowers men's testosterone. The shared study used gold nanoparticles in cells and injected mice. It did not study men wearing rings. Islam's ban rests on authentic Prophetic teaching, not that study.

Claims that pork is uniquely poisonous, side-sleeping cures disease, or prayer replaces medicine also exceed sound evidence. Honey and black seed have research interest, but neither is a universal cure.

- [Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33281445/)

sections.title: Health and Worship
sections.body: Islam joins worship of Allah to sobriety, restraint, cleanliness, family duty, community, rest, and avoiding preventable harm. Research strongly supports some practices and offers promising support for others. This harmony shows Islam as a coherent way of life. Muslims follow revelation, study creation honestly, accept sound medicine, and refuse exaggeration.

quranVerses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُم بِذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ ۗ أَلَا بِذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ ٱلْقُلُوبُ
quranVerses.translation: Those who have believed and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of Allah. Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ
quranVerses.translation: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ هُدًۭى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْهُدَىٰ وَٱلْفُرْقَانِ ۚ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ ٱلشَّهْرَ فَلْيَصُمْهُ ۖ وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ فَعِدَّةٌۭ مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ ۗ يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلْعُسْرَ وَلِتُكْمِلُوا۟ ٱلْعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمْ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ
quranVerses.translation: The month of Ramadhan [is that] in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for the people and clear proofs of guidance and criterion. So whoever sights [the new moon of] the month, let him fast it; and whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days. Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship and [wants] for you to complete the period and to glorify Allah for that [to] which He has guided you; and perhaps you will be grateful.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَا ٱلْخَمْرُ وَٱلْمَيْسِرُ وَٱلْأَنصَابُ وَٱلْأَزْلَٰمُ رِجْسٌۭ مِّنْ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ فَٱجْتَنِبُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ
quranVerses.translation: O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, sacrificing on stone altars to other than Allah, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: ۞ يَٰبَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ خُذُوا۟ زِينَتَكُمْ عِندَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍۢ وَكُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ وَلَا تُسْرِفُوٓا۟ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ
quranVerses.translation: O children of Adam, take your adornment at every masjid, and eat and drink, but be not excessive. Indeed, He likes not those who commit excess.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا۟ ٱلزِّنَىٰٓ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ فَٰحِشَةًۭ وَسَآءَ سَبِيلًۭا
quranVerses.translation: And do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse. Indeed, it is ever an immorality and is evil as a way.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

faq.question: Is salah the same as meditation?
faq.answer: No. Salah is revealed worship with recitation, remembrance, standing, bowing, and prostration. It may share features with attention practices, but its purpose is submission to Allah.

faq.question: Does scientific evidence prove that Islam is true?
faq.answer: No. Science can show benefits or agreement with observations. It cannot alone establish God, prophethood, or revelation. Islam rests on its wider case: Tawhid, the Quran, Muhammad ﷺ, history, reason, and guidance.

faq.question: Is Ramadan fasting safe for everyone?
faq.answer: No. The Quran grants concessions for illness and travel. Islamic law also considers pregnancy, nursing, frailty, and serious risk. Medical conditions require qualified clinical and religious advice.

faq.question: Does wearing gold lower a man's testosterone?
faq.answer: No reliable human evidence shows that ordinary gold jewelry lowers testosterone. The shared experiment used nanoparticles in cells and mice, not rings worn by men. The ruling rests on authentic Prophetic teaching.

faq.question: Can worship replace medical or psychological treatment?
faq.answer: No. Muslims rely on Allah while using lawful means, including qualified medical and psychological care. Prayer, Quran, community, and healthy habits can support treatment, but are not guaranteed substitutes.
